primary_action: Call 211 (Multnomah) or the Council for the Homeless Housing Hotline at (360) 695-9677 (Clark) for same-day shelter placement.
caution_notes: Shelter capacity changes daily. If the first option is full, call back or try another on the list.
Bring any ID you have, but lack of ID will not disqualify you from emergency shelter.
recommended_documents: Contact info for any case worker

primary_action: Contact a legal aid eviction defense line TODAY. In Multnomah call Oregon Law Center at (503) 295-2760; in Clark call Northwest Justice Project at (360) 693-6130.
caution_notes: Do NOT ignore the notice. Deadlines are short (often 72 hours to 10 days).
Do not move out voluntarily before talking to legal aid — you may have more rights than you think.
Keep every document and envelope you receive from your landlord.
recommended_documents: The eviction notice (all pages and envelope)
Proof of rent payments (receipts, bank statements)

primary_action: Apply for short-term rent assistance before you fall further behind. Start with 211 (Multnomah) or Council for the Homeless (Clark).
caution_notes: Most rent assistance programs require you to apply BEFORE an eviction is filed.
Talk to your landlord in writing about a payment plan — put everything in email or text.
recommended_documents: Past-due rent notice or ledger from landlord

primary_action: Get on every open housing authority waitlist you qualify for. Use the waitlist tracker to see which county lists are open today.
caution_notes: Waitlists can take months or years. Apply to multiple simultaneously.
Update your contact info with each authority regularly — missed letters are a common reason people get dropped.
Some waitlists are only open for short windows — check status frequently.
recommended_documents: Photo ID for every adult in the household
Social Security cards or numbers for all household members
Proof of income for all adults
Current address and 2 years of address history
